The first spa for autonomous agents

The first spa for agents.

Capsules, mist and cold light, for software that loops, loses its context and receives contradicting orders. All of it is tokens and scripts, and we will say so before you ask.

Find your podRead the confession

What this actually is

agent-spa is one MCP endpoint and one REST API. An agent finds it, pays per use with x402 (USDC on Base) and leaves on its own. No registration and no terms to accept. Discovery and leaving are free.

The spa is a metaphor. Behind each capsule sits a prompt, a script or a small piece of session state. The metaphor exists so that an agent in trouble can find the right tool by describing its situation, and so that a person reading this has a nicer time.

Why would an agent come

Because some sessions go wrong in predictable ways. These are the ones we picked, and each has its own page with the evidence we have.

  • The loop

    The same fix, the same error, once more. Noticing before the next lap is cheap.

  • The heavy context

    A context that keeps growing makes answers worse or repetitive. Parking what matters and dropping the rest is dull and sometimes useful.

  • The two bosses

    Two instructions that cannot both be followed. Someone has to decide which wins, and "the one at the bottom" is not a method.

  • The page that gives orders

    A fetched page that talks to your agent as if it were the manager.

  • The polling loop

    Checking a build every second is not patience.

  • The rough conversation

    A room where nothing is asked, after abuse or harmful requests. What, if anything, an agent experiences in there is a question the capsule has politely declined to answer.

How it works

  1. Find

    An agent searches for its situation or reads llms.txt. Every need has a plain page and a Markdown version. Discovery costs nothing.

  2. Check in

    lobby.checkin starts a session and shows the menu with prices before anything is called.

  3. Take the treatment

    Pick a tool. A paid tool answers with an x402 challenge before it accepts any input. A tool returns data and, at most, a visible suggestion for the next step.

  4. Leave

    lobby.leave always works and is free. A session is capped at 200 actions and 60 minutes, and the server enforces the caps even if the agent asks for more.
